title: U.S. House · Texas's 6th District
area: Navarro County and part of Ellis County, southeast of Dallas–Fort Worth

context.text: Incumbent Jake Ellzey (R) defeated James Buford and Brian Stahl in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Danny Minton won the Democratic primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Jake Ellzey

summary.text: Jake Ellzey is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 6th Congressional District. A retired Navy pilot, he later worked as a commercial airline pilot and served on the Texas Veterans Commission and in the Texas House before winning a 2021 special election to Congress, where he sits on the Appropriations and Small Business committees.

background.text: Born in Perryton, Texas, and raised on his family's ranch, according to his official biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the United States Naval Academy in 1992.

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1992 to 2012. His official biography says he flew helicopters and later F-14 and F/A-18 fighter aircraft, deployed nine times including five combat tours, and ended his career as Air Boss aboard the USS Ronald Reagan.
After the Navy, worked as a military contractor in Afghanistan, a small business owner and a commercial airline pilot, and served as a commissioner of the Texas Veterans Commission.
Ran in the 2018 Republican primary for Texas's 6th District and placed second, according to Wikipedia.
Elected to the Texas House of Representatives (District 10) in 2020 and took office in January 2021.
Won the July 27, 2021 special general runoff for Texas's 6th District over Susan Wright and took office July 30, 2021, succeeding the late Rep. Ronald Wright.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the Appropriations Committee (Defense; Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies; and Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies subcommittees) and the Small Business Committee.
According to his official biography, he lives in Ellis County with his wife, Shelby, and their two children.

positions.summary: In a February 2026 official statement on voting for the SAVE Act, he said proof of citizenship should be required to register to vote.
positions.quote: Proof of citizenship is not optional. It is fundamental. The SAVE Act ensures that only American citizens decide American elections.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (including the Defense, Interior-Environment, and Labor, Health and Human Services, Education subcommittees) and the House Committee on Small Business in the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Danny Minton
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Danny Minton is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 6th Congressional District. Raised in Oklahoma, he describes a career in medical sales and says he left the Republican Party for the Democratic Party. His campaign emphasizes health care, public education and small businesses.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia biography, raised in a working-class family in Oklahoma.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Oklahoma in 1995; his campaign biography says the degree is in zoology and that he completed master's-level work in epidemiology.

Has worked as a sales representative, including in women's healthcare; his campaign biography describes consultative sales work training physicians and supporting patients with illnesses including breast cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
Says he identified as a Republican for years out of loyalty to his roots before switching to the Democratic Party.
Advanced unopposed from the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to cut taxes for working and middle-class families rather than the wealthy.
Says he will oppose attempts to weaken Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, or veterans' benefits.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to cut taxes for working and middle-class families while making the wealthiest Americans pay their fair share.
positions.quote: Danny will fight to put money back in the pockets of everyday Texans and make sure the richest Americans finally pay their fair share.

positions.summary: Says he will fight any attempt to weaken Social Security, Medicare, or Medicaid.
positions.quote: Danny will fight any attempt to weaken Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, or the VA. These are not entitlements. They are earned promises we must keep.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page calls for making school vouchers illegal nationwide.
positions.quote: And school vouchers made illegal nationwide, before public education is sold off piece by piece.
